The explicit spectral bound establishes at least six bad bonds; Shrikhande and rook witness spin arrays achieve six and eight, and the rook row/column K4 argument forbids fewer than eight. Two algorithmically independent exact full-state enumerations each cover 3^16 labeled configurations per graph and agree on every one of 34 fixed-occupancy minima and counts, compiled from actual accompanying paths. The rational supporting lines give all claimed transition values and degeneracies, including collinear sectors; no sampling or infinite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The two classical nonisomorphic cospectral (16,6,2,2) graphs form a classical spectral-indistinguishability benchmark. Their 3-color antiferromagnetic physical responses differ in ground cost, total residual degeneracy, and four versus six field crossings. The spectral frustration bound is achieved for one and obstructed by rook clique geometry for the other. The full finite field classification is a complete natural invariant and provides an explicit reproducible benchmark; it does not assert a bulk theorem.
